requirements.evidence: Contract implemented in full: `CreateQueue::__invoke(Entity, User, string, ?string)` (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:17), `UpdateQueue::__invoke(..., ?string $name, ?string $slug, ?bool $isActive)` with named-arg calls in tests (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:16, tests/Feature/Queue/UpdateQueueTest.php:28), `SetQueueAccess::__invoke` (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:18), `QueuePermission::Call` (app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:5), `QueueAccess` table/cast/relations (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:23,28,38,46), all four policy abilities (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:17,27,37,44), both call paths authorized (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32; app/Models/Ticket.php:101-105 inactive check before authorize before the waiting check), no delete action, and docs/CHANGELOG updated. Deductions: the race path only recognises MySQL/SQLite unique errors (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:69-77, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:84-92) and the policy relies on `User::membershipFor()` / `App\Models\UserRole` which the diff never introduces (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:10,46).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes live in `app/Actions/*` and authorize inside the action (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:19, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:18, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:26); migration is generator-style with docblocks and a reversible `down()` (database/migrations/2026_10_29_053156_create_queue_access_table.php:12-30); deliberate fillable via `#[Fillable]` matching `Ticket` (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:11); docs `business-rules.md`, `database-schema.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` Added section all updated. Deviations: no PHPDoc on the new public `__invoke` methods (conventions ask for PHPDoc on touched public methods) and empty constructors in all three actions (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:15).

security.evidence: Every write path authorizes server-side via `Gate::forUser(...)->authorize` (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:19, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:18, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:26) and both call paths enforce `call` (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32, app/Models/Ticket.php:105); all input is validated before persisting (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:22-35, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:28-34); attributes are explicit, so no mass-assignment exposure; a corrupted non-array `permissions` value denies (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:57-59). Gap: the cross-entity `ValidationException` is thrown before the authorization check (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:20 vs :26), so a non-manager can distinguish a matching membership/queue pair from a mismatched one.

tests.evidence: New Pest suites cover happy paths plus authorization failures: create (tests/Feature/Queue/CreateQueueTest.php:88), update (tests/Feature/Queue/UpdateQueueTest.php:97), grants/revokes including self-grant and no-log revoke (tests/Feature/Queue/SetQueueAccessTest.php:76,108), policy including corrupted permissions (tests/Feature/Queue/QueuePolicyTest.php:77) and unauthorized calls in every mode (tests/Feature/Queue/QueuePolicyTest.php:112); existing `CallNextTicketTest` was adapted with memberships, not weakened. Missing: a member of another entity on update (tests/Feature/Queue/UpdateQueueTest.php:97 only uses an employee and a stranger) and the DB-unique-index race branch.

simplicity.evidence: Good reuse of `Gate`, `updateOrCreate`, `Str::slug` and factories, but the slug-taken query, length checks and `isUniqueViolation()` are duplicated almost verbatim between app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:29-71 and app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:35-92; the three actions also carry dead empty constructors (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:15, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:14, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:16).

readability.evidence: Clear names and small focused methods; useful docblocks on the policy (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:12-43), the model (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:18-22) and the factory (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:12-20). Minor noise: an unnecessary `$queue->refresh()` after `update()` (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:72) and the afterMaking FK juggling in database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:33-60.

scope.evidence: The diff only contains the queue/access domain (actions, policy, enum, model, factory, migration), the two call paths it must guard (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32, app/Models/Ticket.php:96-108), their tests, and the three docs the task names (CHANGELOG.md:9, docs/business-rules.md:99-101, docs/database-schema.md:5). No UI, no extra permissions, no delete action.

issues.explanation: The policy calls `$user->membershipFor((int) $queue->entity_id)`, but the change never adds that method to `App\Models\User`, and the previous `Ticket::call()` looked membership up with a direct query, so this dependency cannot be verified from the diff; if it does not exist, every policy check fatals.

`use App\Models\UserRole;` is used for enum-like cases (`UserRole::Owner`, `UserRole::Admin`), while every other enum in the project lives in `App\Enums` (app/Models/Ticket.php:5-6, app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:3); if `UserRole` is `App\Enums\UserRole`, the import is wrong and the policy fails.

`isUniqueViolation()` only matches SQLSTATE `23000` and the case-sensitive fragments `UNIQUE`/`Duplicate`, so on PostgreSQL (SQLSTATE `23505`, lower-case "duplicate key value") a race still escapes as a raw `QueryException` instead of the `ValidationException` requirement 2 demands; the same code is duplicated at app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:84.

The membership/queue entity comparison runs before `authorize('manageAccess')`, so an employee or outsider can tell a matching pair from a mismatched one by the exception type (`ValidationException` vs `AuthorizationException`), leaking which membership belongs to which entity.
The update authorization test covers an employee and a complete stranger but not a member of another entity, which requirement 5 names explicitly alongside them.
No test exercises the DB-unique-index race branch (`QueryException` -> `ValidationException`, app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:50), an explicit requirement; only the pre-check is covered.

Slug-taken lookup, length validation and `isUniqueViolation()` are copy-pasted into app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:35-92; a shared helper or a `Rule::unique()`-based validator would remove roughly forty duplicated lines.
`public function __construct() {}` is dead code in all three actions (CreateQueue, UpdateQueue, SetQueueAccess); PHP already provides an argument-less constructor.
`$queue->refresh()` costs an extra query; `$queue->update()` already writes the new attributes onto the in-memory model.
The new public `__invoke()` methods have no PHPDoc, while the project asks for PHPDoc on touched public methods (the policy and model methods in this change do document theirs).

The `afterMaking` hook creates Entity/membership/queue rows, so even `QueueAccess::factory()->make()` silently hits the database; a `definition()` default (or a shared state) would be less surprising.

review.summary: The change implements the whole queue lifecycle, the `queue_access` grant table/action, the `QueuePolicy` single source of truth and `call` enforcement on both call paths, with thorough Pest coverage and the three required docs updated. It is close to approvable, but the policy depends on `User::membershipFor()` and a `UserRole` import that the diff never establishes (both would be fatal if wrong), the unique-violation fallback does not cover PostgreSQL races, and the grant action validates before it authorizes.
